body_ar:
ما هي حقيقة الكشف ولمن يكون؟

أن الكشف معناه أن يكشف الله تعالى لبعض عباده شيئا من الغيوب النسبية، فالغيب قسمان غيب حقيقي وهذا لا يكشف لأحد لأنه من علم الله الذي استأثر به كما قال الله تعالى: {وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ}[الأنعام 59] وقال النبي (ص) في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ}[لقمان 34] فهذا الغيب الحقيقي لا اطلاع لأحد من المخلوقات عليه وهو من خصائص الإله جل جلاله،

النوع الثاني هو الغيب النسبي وهو الذي يطلع عليه بعض العباد دون بعض، فالاطلاع عليه بالوسائل المعهودة غير خارق للعادة، كاطلاع الطبيب على حال الجنين في بطن أمه أنه حي يتنفس، أو أنه ذكر أو أنثى أو نحو ذلك بواسطة الأشعة فهذا اطلاع بأمور عادية كما إذا ذبحت الشاة وسلخت فشق بطنها فإذا فيه جنين فقد كان قبل الكشف عليه غيبا نسبيا وبعد الكشف عليه أصبح من عالم الشهادة، فهذا النوع من الغيوب النسبية،

ومثل ذلك من كان وراء هذا الجدار الآن لا يرى من دونه، لكن هذا الغيب غيب نسبي لأنه إذا دخل من الباب رآهم فانكشف له ما كان مغيبا عنه، ومثل ذلك ما يحصل عن طريق الأجهزة كالكلام بالهاتف مع إنسان بعيد، أو رؤيته عن طريق الأقمار الصناعة، أو بالهاتف المرئي فهذا من الغيب النسبي واكتشافه حينئذ بالوسائل المعتادة غير خارق للعادة،

أما انكشافه بالخارق للعادة من غير وسائل أصلا نراها، فهذا هو الكشف بمعنى خرق العادة، أن يرى الإنسان ما لا يراه غيره في الأمور العادية، مثلا إذا نظر الإنسان بمكبر فرأى هلالا أو نجما بعيدا هذا غير خارق للعادة لأنه كشف له غيب نسبي بآلة ووسيلة إذا رآه من غير آلة فهذا خارق للعادة فهو كشف لذلك الغيب النسبي،

وهذا الكشف قد يكون كرامة يكرم الله بها بعض أوليائه فيطلعهم على بعض الأمور التي تزيدهم إيمانا وخشية لله وزيادة توكل عليه ومحبة له، وقد يكون فتنة كما يبتلي الله به بعض المخرفين فيطلعهم على بعض الغيوب النسبية فيرون بذلك أنهم يتصرفون في الكون أو أنهم يؤثرون بما ليس لهم، فيدعون الدعاوي الباطلة الكاذبة فهذا فتنة عليهم،

ومثل ذلك يحصل للمؤمن والكافر، فهذا الكشف يحصل للمؤمنين ويحصل للكافرين ويحصل لمن لا يدعي الإسلام أصلا، كثير من النصارى واليهود يحصل لهم هذا النوع من الكشوف، وأعظمه فتنة على أهل الأرض ما يحصل منه للمسيح الدجال،

فالمسيح الدجال يحصل له من الكشوف الشيء العجيب جدا، فيري الإنسان والده وأمه وقد ماتا من فترة ويسمعه كلامهما ويمر على القرية الخربة فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل ويأتي أهل القرية وهم مسنتون فيصدقونه فيأمر السماء فتمطر ويأمر الأرض فتنبت، فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم أسمن ما كانت ضروعا، ويمر على أهل قرية وهم في خصب فيكذبونه فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقلع فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم وهي في أشد اللأواء، فهذا من الكشوفات التي تحصل للمسيح الدجال،

وبهذا يعلم أن الكشف ليس علامة من علامات الولاية لله، أنه يحصل للمؤمنين ويحصل للكافرين ويحصل لأعداء الله ويحصل لأولياء الله كل بحسب ما يؤتيه الله منه، وما يحصل منه لأولياء الله هو ما يزيدهم إيمانا وتوكلا على الله ومحبة له فهذا هو الذي يكون كرامة، أما ما ليس كذلك كما يزيد الإنسان طغيانا وأن يدعي أنه يتصرف في الكون فهذا ليس كشفا محمودا وليس كرامة.
body_en:
What is the reality of unveiling (kashf), and to whom does it occur?

Unveiling means that God, exalted, unveils to some of His servants something of the relative unseen. The unseen is of two kinds. There is a real unseen, and this is not unveiled to anyone, because it is of God's knowledge which He has kept to Himself, as God, exalted, said: {And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He} [الأنعام 59] (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:59). And the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said, concerning five which none knows but God: {Indeed, God — with Him is knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die} [لقمان 34] (Sūrat Luqmān 31:34). This real unseen — no created being has any access to it, and it is among the exclusive properties of the Deity, majestic is His majesty.

The second kind is the relative unseen: that which some servants come to know and others do not. Coming to know it by the accustomed means is not a break with the customary order — as with a physician's coming to know the state of the foetus in its mother's belly, that it is alive and breathing, or that it is male or female, or the like, by means of imaging. This is coming to know by ordinary things; just as when a sheep is slaughtered and skinned and its belly is opened and there is a foetus in it: before it was uncovered it was a relative unseen, and after it was uncovered it became part of the world of the witnessed. This is of the kind of the relative unseen.

Likewise, whoever is behind this wall now is not seen by the one on the other side of it; but this unseen is a relative unseen, because if he comes in through the door he sees them, and what had been hidden from him is unveiled to him. And likewise what occurs by means of devices, such as speaking by telephone with a distant person, or seeing him by means of satellites, or by video telephone. This is of the relative unseen, and its discovery in that case, by the accustomed means, is not a break with the customary order.

But its being unveiled by a break with the customary order, with no means at all that we can see — this is unveiling in the sense of a break with the customary order: that a person sees what others do not see in ordinary matters. For instance, if a person looks through a magnifying glass and sees a crescent moon or a distant star, that is not a break with the customary order, because a relative unseen was unveiled to him by an instrument and a means; but if he sees it without an instrument, then that is a break with the customary order, and it is an unveiling of that relative unseen.

This unveiling may be a charism with which God honours some of His friends, disclosing to them certain matters that increase them in faith and in awe of God, and in greater reliance upon Him and love for Him. And it may be a trial, as God tries with it some of the deluded, disclosing to them some of the relative unseen, so that they take themselves to be disposing of the universe, or to be exercising an influence that is not theirs, and so make false and lying claims. This is a trial upon them.

The like of this happens to the believer and to the unbeliever. This unveiling happens to believers, and happens to unbelievers, and happens to one who makes no claim to Islam at all: many of the Christians and the Jews have this kind of unveiling happen to them. And the greatest of it as a trial upon the people of the earth is what happens of it to the False Messiah.

For the False Messiah has the most astonishing unveilings happen to him. He shows a person his father and his mother, who died some time ago, and lets him hear their speech. He passes by the ruined village and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. He comes to the people of a village who are in drought and they believe him, so he commands the sky and it rains, and commands the earth and it brings forth growth, and their livestock come home to them in the evening with their udders fuller than they have ever been. And he passes by the people of a village who are in plenty and they call him a liar, so he commands the sky and it withholds, and commands the earth and it is stripped bare, and their livestock come home to them in the severest hardship. This is of the unveilings that happen to the False Messiah.

By this it is known that unveiling is not one of the signs of friendship with God — that it happens to believers and happens to unbelievers, and happens to the enemies of God and happens to the friends of God, each according to what God gives him of it. What happens of it to the friends of God is what increases them in faith, in reliance upon God and in love for Him; this is what constitutes a charism. As for what is not like that — such as what increases a person in overweening insolence, and his claiming that he disposes of the universe — this is not a praiseworthy unveiling, and is not a charism.

flags.context: أن الكشف معناه أن يكشف الله تعالى لبعض عباده شيئا من الغيوب النسبية
flags.note: kashf is the organising term of the whole answer and recurs throughout. Option 2 must be avoided: the Sheikh's entire point is that kashf is NOT a mark of sainthood and occurs to unbelievers and to the Dajjal, so a rendering that builds a Sufi valuation into the word would reverse his argument. Whichever is fixed must be used consistently wherever kashf appears in the corpus.

flags.context: وقد يكون فتنة كما يبتلي الله به بعض المخرفين
flags.note: Unvowelled in the source. Read as al-mukharrifīn (from خرف, to drivel or be senile) it means those whose talk is delusion, which is how it has been rendered; read as al-mukharrifīn in the sense of fabricators it would come closer to 'charlatans', which implies deliberate deceit. The difference matters: the Sheikh is describing people who are themselves taken in by what is shown to them ('this is a trial upon them'), which tells against the deliberate-deceit reading.

flags.context: ويمر على أهل قرية وهم في خصب فيكذبونه فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقلع
options: and commands the earth and it is stripped bare
and commands the earth and it withholds its growth
and commands the earth and it becomes barren
flags.note: SOURCE VARIATION. The same clause of the same hadith appears three times in this slice with three different verbs: فتقحل in article 522, فتقلع here, and فتقحط in article 539. قحل and قحط both mean to dry up or suffer drought; قلع does not, and is most likely a copying slip for one of them. The source reading has been kept and the English chosen to fit the sense of the passage. A reviewer should decide whether to standardise across the three articles.

flags.arabic: وقال النبي (ص) في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ …}
flags.context: the attribution of the verse of Luqman
options: translate as given — the Prophet said this concerning the five
render so that the words quoted are clearly the Qur'anic verse rather than the Prophet's own words
attribute the verse to God and the framing to the Prophet
flags.note: As printed, the sentence introduces a Qur'anic verse with 'and the Prophet said'. The hadith on 'the keys of the unseen are five' recites this verse, so the Sheikh's phrasing is compressed rather than mistaken — but in English it can read as attributing the words of the Qur'an to the Prophet. The braces mark it as Qur'an, and the reference is supplied, which is why option 1 is recommended over a bare literal rendering.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The source supplies its own sura markers for both Qur'anic quotations ('[الأنعام 59]' and '[لقمان 34]'). Those markers have been kept and the full house references added beside them.
The Sheikh's contemporary examples — ultrasound imaging, the telephone, satellites, video calling, the magnifying glass — are his own and are part of the argument, not glosses added in translation.

The description of the Dajjal reproduces the wording of the long hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Samʿan, given here without narrator, collection or grading. None has been supplied. The same passage recurs in articles 522 and 539 of this slice, each time with small differences of wording; see the flag on فتقلع.
Source spelling preserved verbatim in body_ar: الأقمار الصناعة for الأقمار الصناعية, and الدعاوي for الدعاوى.
